frozen_canary_inputs.source: same label-blind DROID observation and two real distinct candidate-policy traces used only after Phase B data admission

observation_validity_criteria: 17 frames are present for the native 16-action request including the conditioning frame
registered width and height match the pinned runtime geometry contract
RGB color, 15 FPS, and frame timestamps are valid
no collapse category is triggered before the selected advance boundary
policy_requery_success_criteria: the same frozen endpoint receives the exact retained generated observation
one 16x10 finite DROID action chunk is returned
action and request identities are hashed
policy identity never enters the evaluator payload
temporal_alignment_checks: action row i governs transition from frame i to frame i plus 1
the selected boundary frame is reused byte-exactly for the next policy query
derived seconds equal executed steps divided by 15

historical_projection_only.basis: Cosmos3 follow-up post-load mean 3.289976753604909 seconds per request; not a new provider quote

deterministic_selection_rule: Prefer the smallest candidate supported by the exact upstream native DROID autoregressive advance contract; break ties toward fewer WAM calls, then lower projected latency.
selection_basis: The pinned Cosmos DROID contract uses a 16-action chunk at 15 FPS.
The official autoregressive notebook advances all 16 generated frames and conditions the next request on the last generated frame.
The pinned model card declares action inputs of at least 16 frames.
No live endpoint or outcome label was used to choose among candidates.
claim_boundary: This is a prospective contract-derived fallback selection, not an empirical finding that 16 steps optimizes ranking fidelity. The 4/8/16 empirical comparison remains required if eligible live endpoints are later admitted without exposing outcome labels.
